To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a multi-parameter flow cytometric method for assessing the physiological response of bacteria to environmental stresses is feasible.

multi-parameter flow cytometric analysis can be used to study the physiological response of bacteria to environmental changes during cultivations and that the results can be applied to improve the process control of fed-batch processes.

the use of flow cytometry to study physiological responses of E. coli W3110 cells to glucose limitation during small-scale batch, fed-bath and continuous culture cultivatons has shown that there is a considerable reduction in cell viability, as characterised by membrane depolarisation, during the latter stages (high cell densities) of small-scale fed-batch cultivatons.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the application of 'at-line' multi-parameter flow cytometric analysis of bacterial cultivations, to the study of the physiological response of E. coli W3110 during batch, fedbatch and continuous culture cultivatios.
the development and application of flow cytometry for 'at-line' and 'on-line' monitoring of microbial cultivations.
the use of multi-parameter, flow cytometric techniques to characterise the physiological state of bacterial populations during the latter stages (glucose limited growth) of fed-batch cultivatins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physiological state of a cell is a complex phenomenon that can only be fully appreciated by using a range of techniques.

the use of multi-parameter, flow cytometry is a useful and powerful technique for the 'at- and on-line' monitoring of bacterial cultivations and that the technique has a number of advantages over other methods.
the use of multi-parameter cytometry has shown that fed-batch cultivarions are more stressful to E. coli W3110 cells than either batch or continuous cultivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physiological status of the cells in a fed-batch process is more heterogeneous and less stable than that in a batch or continuous culture.

the flow cytometric techniques developed can detect physiological changes within bacterial populations, and that the use of flow cytometry to assess the physiological status of a bacterial population in situ can be used as a valuable tool in the development of improved process control strategies.
the use of multi-parameter cytometry can provide a useful and rapid means of assessing the physiological state of a bacterial culture.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to use a combination of fluorescent stains and flow cytometry to assess the physiological state of a bacterial population, and to monitor the effect of process conditions on cell physiological status.
the physiological response of E. coli is different in batch, fed-bath and continuous cultures, and that these differences can be detected by flow cytometry.
it is possible to assess the physiological status of bacterial cells in real-time using a flow cytometer, which can be used for process monitoring and control.
